lessons.title: The Company, Its Processes and Its Requirements

slots.practicalActivity: Start a requirements document (a plain text file or spreadsheet) and copy into it the LTV Manufacturing Corporation company snapshot, the ten-person stakeholder table (Elena Marsh, Victor Okafor, Sarah Lindqvist, Chen Liu, Mateo Rios, Grace Olsen, Derek Shaw, Marcus Ibarra, Dana Whitfield, Priya Nandan), the four suppliers/three customers/two banks, and Elena Marsh's five numbered requirements exactly as given. Then write your own one-paragraph summary of the company you could read back to a hiring manager.
slots.deliverable: A started requirements document containing the company profile, stakeholder table, supplier/customer/bank list, and Elena Marsh's five numbered requirements, plus a one-paragraph company summary in your own words.

lessons.title: Configuring Ledger, Legal Entity and Business Units

slots.practicalActivity: Diagram LTV's enterprise structure on paper first -- two legal entities, two primary ledgers (USD and CAD), two business units -- exactly as lesson 3 designs it. Then build it for real, in order, in your own Oracle Fusion practice environment: create the LTV Manufacturing Corporation and LTV Manufacturing Canada ULC legal entities, create the LTV US Primary Ledger (USD) and LTV Canada Primary Ledger (CAD), and create the US Manufacturing & Distribution BU and Canada Operations BU. Verify every ledger shows a legal entity assigned and every business unit shows a ledger assigned before moving on.
slots.deliverable: A hand-drawn enterprise-structure diagram, plus two configured legal entities, two primary ledgers, and two business units in your practice environment, with every ledger-to-legal-entity and business-unit-to-ledger link verified.

lessons.title: Configuring the Chart of Accounts and Calendar

slots.practicalActivity: Build LTV's full five-segment chart of accounts (Company, Cost Center, Account, Intercompany, Future) in your practice environment: enter the Company balancing values (1000 US, 2000 Canada), the three cost centers (410 Assembly, 420 Fabrication, 510 Corporate Overhead), and the complete natural-account list including the new account 7850 (Freight Out -- Customer Shipments). Then build the LTV Corporate Calendar as a twelve-period Gregorian fiscal year 2026, and assign both the chart of accounts and calendar to the two primary ledgers you built last hour.
slots.deliverable: A configured five-segment chart of accounts with every real segment value entered, and a twelve-period 2026 calendar, both assigned to the US and Canada primary ledgers.

slots.practicalActivity: Configure all of LTV's remaining master data for real, closing out Chapter 1: the four suppliers (Meridian Bearing Supply Co. with its EFT payment method, Net 30 terms, three-way matching, and preferred-supplier flag; Palmetto Steel & Alloy Supply; Vantage Electrical Components Inc.; Crescent Freight Logistics), the three customers (Harborview Industrial Supply with full credit limit and receipt-method detail; Tidewater Energy Systems; Great Lakes Automation Group under the Canada Operations BU), the two bank accounts (Regions Bank ...7734 and Royal Bank of Canada ...4420, each linked to account 1110 at the correct Company value), and the five fixed asset categories with their useful lives and two asset books (LTV US Corporate Book, LTV Canada Corporate Book).
slots.deliverable: Four configured suppliers, three configured customers, two configured bank accounts, and five fixed asset categories across two asset books, all saved in your practice environment -- Chapter 1's complete foundation.

slots.practicalActivity: Run LTV's first complete procure-to-pay cycle end to end in your practice environment: enter Dana Whitfield's requisition for 50 units of Industrial Pump Bearing PB-4400 ($18,400.00) against account 1000-420-1410-0000-000, convert it to PO-55210 with Meridian Bearing Supply Co., record Priya Nandan's December 28 receipt, enter the December 31 GRNI accrual journal JE-GRNI-1231 (deliberately leaving its auto-reverse flag unchecked, exactly as the lesson describes), enter and validate Meridian's January invoice INV-MER-88341, and build the Payment Process Request paying both Meridian invoices (PMT-21094 for $18,400.00 and PMT-21087 for $9,200.00) by EFT from Regions Bank.
slots.deliverable: A complete requisition-to-payment trail in your practice environment -- PO-55210, the December receipt, JE-GRNI-1231 with its auto-reverse flag left unchecked, invoice INV-MER-88341, and payments PMT-21094/PMT-21087 -- set up exactly as the capstone requires for Chapter 3.

slots.practicalActivity: Run Harborview Industrial Supply's order-to-cash cycle: enter sales order SO-48217 for 400 Model CP-220 Control Panels with the 5% volume discount (net $55,100.00), run AutoInvoice to generate INV-HV-30144 including the freight line to account 7850, and record Harborview's $55,100.00 incoming wire as receipt RCPT-50231. Apply the receipt to the older INV-HV-29890 ($6,100.00) instead of INV-HV-30144, exactly as Mateo Rios does, then pull Harborview's AR aging detail and confirm for yourself that total cash and total AR are unaffected even though the open-item detail is now wrong.
slots.deliverable: Sales order SO-48217, invoice INV-HV-30144, and receipt RCPT-50231 entered in your practice environment, with the receipt deliberately misapplied to INV-HV-29890 and the resulting AR aging detail printed to confirm the effect.

slots.practicalActivity: Capitalize the new CNC lathe as asset FA-10452 ($145,000.00, placed in service January 2) into the LTV US Corporate Book, choosing Office Equipment (5-year life) and cost center 410 exactly as Derek Shaw does. Run January depreciation and confirm your own calculation matches the system's: $145,000.00 / 60 months = $2,416.67. Then calculate on paper what the correct Manufacturing Equipment (10-year life, cost center 420) depreciation would have been, so you have both the as-configured and correct numbers ready for Chapter 3.
slots.deliverable: Asset FA-10452 capitalized and depreciated in your practice environment under the incorrect Office Equipment category, with a side-by-side written calculation of the as-configured $2,416.67 and the correct $1,208.33 monthly depreciation.

lessons.title: Subledger Accounting and General Ledger Posting

slots.practicalActivity: Load January's Regions Bank statement into Cash Management and reconcile it against the GL, confirming the $9,200.00 unexplained variance from the duplicated PMT-21087 transmission stays open. Then run Create Accounting across Payables, Receivables, and Fixed Assets for January, confirm the 14 freight-out Receivables transactions land at accounting status Incomplete ($4,250.00 total, no Account Rule for account 7850), and save -- without submitting -- the $27,750.00 intercompany journal INTERCO-JAN-0131 in Draft status, exactly as Victor Okafor leaves it.
slots.deliverable: A bank reconciliation worksheet showing the open $9,200.00 variance, a Create Accounting run showing 14 Incomplete transactions totaling $4,250.00, and journal INTERCO-JAN-0131 saved in Draft status -- the complete, unresolved state Chapter 2 hands off to Chapter 3.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter lab: before reading Elena Marsh's call, run your own preliminary close checks across the configuration and transactions you built in Chapters 1-2. Pull a trial balance for both ledgers, an AP aging report, an AR aging report by invoice (not just total balance), and the Subledger Accounting accounting events report filtered to Incomplete. Without looking ahead to lesson 18, write down anything that looks off to you, in your own words.
slots.deliverable: Your own preliminary trial balance, AP/AR aging, and SLA status pulls across both ledgers, plus a written list of anything you personally flagged as off before reading Elena Marsh's six symptoms.

lessons.title: The CFO's Call: The Books Do Not Balance

slots.practicalActivity: Write down Elena Marsh's six symptoms from the January 31 call word for word. Then, without looking ahead, compare them against the list you flagged yourself in the previous hour's lab and against your own hypothesis for what might be causing each one, based only on the configuration and transactions you built yourself in Chapters 1 and 2.
slots.deliverable: A written list of Elena Marsh's six symptoms with your own pre-investigation hypothesis for each, checked against what you personally flagged in the previous hour's preliminary close check.

slots.practicalActivity: In your own practice environment, investigate the first three symptoms yourself: pull account 2150's activity for cost center 420 and find both JE-GRNI-1231 and INV-MER-88341's accounting sitting there together; pull Harborview's AR aging detail by invoice and trace RCPT-50231's application history; and open FA-10452's asset record and cross-check its category and cost center against the original capital approval. Confirm each root cause with the actual record before writing anything down as fact.
slots.deliverable: Three written root-cause findings (the unreversed GRNI journal, the misapplied receipt, and the miscategorized asset), each backed by the specific GL or subledger record you pulled to confirm it.

lessons.title: Investigating Cash Management, Subledger Accounting and General Ledger

slots.practicalActivity: Investigate the remaining three symptoms: pull the bank reconciliation worksheet's open item and draft the specific questions you would ask Regions Bank's commercial services desk to confirm a duplicate transmission; run the Subledger Accounting accounting events report filtered to January/Incomplete and confirm all 14 rows are Freight Charge transactions missing an Account Rule for account 7850; and run a journal batch status report for January in both ledgers to find INTERCO-JAN-0131 sitting in Draft.
slots.deliverable: Three written root-cause findings (the bank's duplicate transmission, the missing Account Rule for 7850, and the unposted intercompany journal), each backed by the specific report you ran to confirm it.

lessons.title: Correcting, Reconciling and Completing the Month-End Close

slots.practicalActivity: Apply all six corrections yourself in your practice environment: enter reversing journal JE-REV-0131 for the GRNI accrual; unapply RCPT-50231 from INV-HV-29890 and reapply it correctly to INV-HV-30144; reclassify FA-10452 from Office Equipment/410 to Manufacturing Equipment/420 and confirm depreciation recalculates to $1,208.33; record the bank's $9,200.00 reversal in Cash Management; add the missing Account Rule mapping line for account 7850 and rerun Create Accounting on the 14 Incomplete transactions; and submit INTERCO-JAN-0131 for posting. Finish by rerunning the trial balance for both ledgers and closing period Jan-26.
slots.deliverable: All six corrections applied and verified in your practice environment, a clean trial balance for both the US and Canada ledgers, and period Jan-26 closed in both.

lessons.title: Deliverables: Reports, Issue Log and Implementation Documentation
Final Presentation: What Was Wrong and How It Was Corrected

slots.practicalActivity: Assemble the seven real deliverables Elena Marsh needs: generate the Income Statement and Balance Sheet for period Jan-26, the AP Aging and AR Aging reports, a written reconciliation report covering the bank/GRNI/intercompany ties, a six-row issue log in symptom/root-cause/fix/verified format, and a short implementation-documentation narrative. Then rehearse and record (or deliver to a study partner) the 30-minute findings presentation, structured headline-first and grouping the six issues into the three root-cause patterns the lesson describes.
slots.deliverable: A seven-part deliverables package (two financial statements, two aging reports, a reconciliation report, a six-row issue log, and implementation documentation) plus a recorded or witnessed findings presentation.

lessons.title: Reviewing Your Work Against the Requirements

slots.practicalActivity: Go line by line through Elena Marsh's five original requirements from lesson 2 and write, for each, what you actually built and whether it was met cleanly on the first pass or only after Chapter 3's correction work. Then assemble your four-part capstone portfolio (company and requirements, configuration, operations and crisis, review) into a single document or deck, and write out and rehearse your two-minute spoken answer to 'walk me through a project you're proud of,' using this exact capstone.
slots.deliverable: A five-line requirements-review memo, a complete four-part capstone portfolio document, and a written and rehearsed two-minute project narrative -- ready for the Career & Interview Preparation course and for a real interview.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can configure a complete two-entity Oracle Fusion Financials implementation, run a full month of real transactions across every subledger, and diagnose and correct a genuine six-problem month-end close under deadline pressure -- completing the hands-on, project-based core of the entire Oracle Fusion Financials Consultant path with a portfolio-ready capstone.
